In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of iron in the form of ferrous sulfate is not the most effective form of iron for the treatment of iron-deficiency anemia.
the use of hydrogen-reduced elemental ferrous iron is a safe, efficient, and effective way to fortify wheat products.
the iron fortification of wheat products with electrolytic iron or with hydrogen-reduced elemental is more effective than the use of ferrous sulfate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a hydrogen reduced iron (Hi-Fe) in a wheat-based snack food is a promising approach to increase iron absorption and iron stores, especially in women.

the use of iron supplements and iron-fortified foods can be a successful approach to reduce iron deficiency anemia and its complications in pregnant women and children in low- and middle-income countries.
the use of a combination of different iron compounds in a food matrix may provide a more efficacious and better-tolerated source of iron for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia.
